title: Inquest into death of Winnipeg teen after police Tasered him makes no recommendations
subtitle: Michael Langan, 17, was stunned by police officers in an alley in July 2008
article: The father of a teen who died after being shocked by a police stun gun is upset the judge for the inquest found police acted appropriately and nothing could have been done differently to prevent his son's death.
Brian Minchin reacts to the judge's findings in the inquest into the death of his son, Michael Langan.
"I've been suffering for eight years already, I'll suffer for the rest of my life. I didn't only lose my son I [lost] everything else," said Brian Minchin, Langan's father.
"I have no opportunity to see him get married or to have any grandchildren now. That's all just taken away."
Langan said it took too long to get through the inquest. The inquest report was released this week.
"There are no recommendations that I can make to prevent similar deaths from occurring in the future," provincial court judge Timothy Killeen concluded.
At the time officers came across Langan, they were searching for a robbery suspect. They said Langan was holding a knife and refused to put it down.

The inquest report says one of the officers, Const. Michael Temple, stepped out of the car and drew his gun, pointing it at Langan. The teen, who was standing about five feet from the passenger side of the police cruiser, spun around, holding the knife out.

Temple considered shooting Langan, who he described as having an angry, crazed look on his face, as if Langan was under the influence of alcohol or drugs and staring right through him, the report states.

Temple said he also feared for the life of his partner, Const. Ryan Naismith, who was in the passenger side of the car. If Langan rushed the vehicle, Naismith would not have been able to get away. There was a protective glass separating the front seats from the back seat and a computer between the two front seats.
And Naismith could not get out of the car without being right beside Langan, who could have attacked him with almost no movement forward, the inquest report states.
At some point, Naismith had taken out the stun gun and aimed it out of the passenger side window. Seeing that, Temple yelled at him to "Taze" Langan, the report states.

After police fired the stun gun, Langan fell and banged his head. Naismith got out of the car and kicked the teen's knife away. The officers called an ambulance because Langan was bleeding from the head and having trouble breathing.
He was taken to the Health Sciences Centre and pronounced dead.

"I think it was excessive use of force by police. Two warnings is not enough," Minchin said. "They should have tried to talk to him longer. You know, tell him to drop to the ground or something...one cop was yelling 'taze him taze him', for what?"
"It shouldn't have happened in the first place. I think the cops overreacted. My son was a five-foot-three, five-foot-four, 120-pound kid. What they can't try and disarm him?"

An autopsy found Langan died from cardiac arrhythmia likely caused by an undiagnosed rare heart tumour as well as physical and emotional stress from the situation. It also showed the teen was intoxicated and had marijuana in his system.
"The Taser has not been shown to have caused Mr. Langan's death," Killeen's report states.
"The Taser was an appropriate weapon to use in these circumstances. Pepper spray was not immediately available. A device such as a baton could not have been used in time had Mr. Langan moved forward.

"Const. Temple was in a position where he would have been ready to use his handgun in a moment, but the Taser is not a lethal force option like a handgun. No one could be expected to know that a person with a knife might also have a rare heart tumour."
"The death of such a young man was tragic, but nothing in the actions of the police or paramedics contributed to the death," Killeen concludes.

"The use of the Taser was appropriate given the threat presented and the failure of Mr. Langan to respond to the police by dropping the knife. The officers responded to the threat in an appropriate fashion."
